author: Vox
description:
New numbers show that 62% of Latinos now think that Trump wants to deport undocumented immigrants broadly, which is up 26 percentage points from where voters were at the election. But why didn’t they think so in 2024? 

Co-founder and president of Equis Research, Stephanie Valencia, explains on this week’s episode of America, Actually. Watch here on YouTube or listen wherever you get your podcasts.

title: How deportations changed Latinos’ minds on Trump

author: Vox
description:
Latino voters have often been called a "sleeping giant" in US politics, but Equis Research co-founder Stephanie Valencia says that’s wrong: they’re a "swinging giant.” This dynamic, independent-leaning electorate is actively redefining national politics. And now, many of the Latino voters who helped propel President Donald Trump to the White House in 2024 are  having second thoughts. 

In this episode of America, Actually, Vox’s Astead Herndon breaks down the dramatic decline in Trump’s approval rating among the group, the myth of the "monolithic" Latino vote, and how unforced errors in Spanish-language campaigning can leave crucial swing voters on the table. Later, Colorado congressional candidate Manny Rutinel discusses how he’s campaigning in a 40% Latino battleground district.
